proofs.proof_tex:
Assume that \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\ne\varnothing\).  For each \(G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\), define the proof-local feasible set
\[
K_G(p)=\{\lambda\in\Lambda_G:P_G(\lambda)=p\}
\]
and the set of observationally feasible refinements
\[
\mathfrak G_p=\{G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S):K_G(p)\ne\varnothing\}.
\tag{1}
\]
These are abbreviations inside the proof, not additions to the causal target.

Fix \(G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\).  Apply \(\text{lem:finite-factor-support-reduction}\) with a singleton query index set whose sole query is the micro CDE in \(\text{def:micro-cde}\).  If \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(G,p)\), the forward part of that lemma supplies a raw canonical branch and independent factor weights \(\lambda\in\Lambda_G\) for which
\[
P_G(\lambda)=p,
\qquad
q_G(\lambda)=q(\mathcal M).
\tag{2}
\]
The first equality in (2) uses \(\text{ass:observed-law-compatibility}\), and the second uses preservation of the specified interventional query by the finite-support reduction.  Thus \(\lambda\in K_G(p)\).

Conversely, let \(\lambda\in K_G(p)\).  By the converse part of \(\text{lem:finite-factor-support-reduction}\), the branch's deterministic tables and factor weights reconstruct a finite binary semi-Markovian SCM \(\mathcal M_\lambda\) on \(G\).  It satisfies \(\text{ass:structural-recursion}\), and drawing the private and pairwise edge parents from their separate simplex factors gives exactly \(\text{ass:independent-edge-latents}\).  The defining equality \(P_G(\lambda)=p\) supplies \(\text{ass:observed-law-compatibility}\).  Hence \(\mathcal M_\lambda\in\mathfrak M(G,p)\).  The observational and interventional recursions used by \(\text{def:raw-polynomial-compiler}\) are the recursions of this reconstructed SCM, so
\[
q(\mathcal M_\lambda)=q_G(\lambda).
\tag{3}
\]
Equations (2)--(3) prove, including when both sides are empty,
\[
\{q(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(G,p)\}
=\{q_G(\lambda):\lambda\in K_G(p)\}.
\tag{4}
\]

Taking the union of (4) over all refinements and invoking \(\text{def:summary-fiber}\) and \(\text{def:sharp-envelope}\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)
&=\bigcup_{G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}
  \{q_G(\lambda):\lambda\in K_G(p)\}\\
&=\bigcup_{G\in\mathfrak G_p}
  \{q_G(\lambda):\lambda\in K_G(p)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
The second equality deletes only empty sets.  Because the original SCM fiber is nonempty, its image under \(q\) is nonempty; (5) therefore shows that \(\mathfrak G_p\ne\varnothing\).

It remains to prove that all extrema written in the corrected display exist.  For a fixed branch \(r\in\mathcal R_G\), put
\[
\Lambda_{G,r}=\prod_a\Delta(\mathcal K_{G,r,a}).
\]
There are finitely many factors \(a\), and every \(\mathcal K_{G,r,a}\) is finite.  Each probability simplex is a closed and bounded subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, hence compact; therefore the finite product \(\Lambda_{G,r}\) is compact.  By \(\text{def:raw-polynomial-compiler}\), the restriction of \(P_G\) to this branch is polynomial and thus continuous.  Consequently
\[
K_{G,r}(p)=\{\lambda\in\Lambda_{G,r}:P_G(\lambda)=p\}
\tag{6}
\]
is closed in \(\Lambda_{G,r}\) and is compact.  The raw catalogue \(\mathcal R_G\) is finite, so \(K_G(p)\), the disjoint union of the sets in (6), is a finite union of compact branch sets and is compact.  The objective \(q_G\) is polynomial and continuous on every branch by \(\text{def:raw-polynomial-compiler}\).  Hence, whenever \(G\in\mathfrak G_p\), the nonempty compact set \(K_G(p)\) has points \(\lambda_G^-\) and \(\lambda_G^+\) satisfying
\[
q_G(\lambda_G^-)=\min_{\lambda\in K_G(p)}q_G(\lambda),
\qquad
q_G(\lambda_G^+)=\max_{\lambda\in K_G(p)}q_G(\lambda).
\tag{7}
\]

By \(\text{lem:finite-refinements}\), \(\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) is finite.  Its nonempty subset \(\mathfrak G_p\) is therefore finite and nonempty.  Taking the least and greatest of the finitely many attained values in (7), equation (5) and the endpoint definitions in \(\text{def:sharp-envelope}\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\underline q(p)
&=\min_{\substack{G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\\K_G(p)\ne\varnothing}}
  \min_{\lambda\in K_G(p)}q_G(\lambda),\\
\overline q(p)
&=\max_{\substack{G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\\K_G(p)\ne\varnothing}}
  \max_{\lambda\in K_G(p)}q_G(\lambda).
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Replacing the proof-local abbreviation \(K_G(p)\) in (8) by \(\{\lambda\in\Lambda_G:P_G(\lambda)=p\}\) is exactly the displayed formula in the corrected statement.  In particular, no minimum or maximum is taken over an empty set.

Finally, the converse construction used in (3) applies to every feasible response-weight point, including the four levels of optimizers in (7)--(8).  It assigns one mutually independent finite exogenous variable to each private index and each displayed pairwise bidirected-edge index.  Several pairwise parents may be incident to the same observed vertex, but they remain distinct independent factors, so overlapping latent-parent incidence is preserved exactly.  Conversely, (2) represents every compatible SCM with the same observed law and micro CDE.  Thus (5) is equality of attainable images, the endpoints in (8) are attained by compatible SCMs, and the interval is sharp rather than merely a valid outer bound.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every nonempty fiber \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\),
\[
[\underline q(p),\overline q(p)]
=\left[
\min_{\substack{G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\\ \{\lambda\in\Lambda_G:P_G(\lambda)=p\}\ne\varnothing}}\ \min_{\lambda\in\Lambda_G:P_G(\lambda)=p}q_G(\lambda),
\ \max_{\substack{G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\\ \{\lambda\in\Lambda_G:P_G(\lambda)=p\}\ne\varnothing}}\ \max_{\lambda\in\Lambda_G:P_G(\lambda)=p}q_G(\lambda)
\right].
\]
Both extrema are attained. Every feasible response-weight point reconstructs a semi-Markovian SCM with the displayed independent overlapping pairwise latent parents, and every compatible SCM has a raw canonical response-weight representative with the same \((p,q)\) image.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Nonemptiness of the union fiber guarantees at least one feasible refinement, but it does not make every refinement compatible with \(p\). In the current nested display an incompatible refinement has an empty inner feasible set, so its ordinary minimum and maximum are undefined. Restricting the outer extrema to refinements with a nonempty canonical fiber deletes only empty image components and makes the exact sharp-envelope formula total.

proposed.comparator_claim: Their controlled-effect theorem identifies the micro CDE by an unadjusted conditional-mean contrast when the outcome is in no nontrivial directed cycle and has no bidirected edge to a directed ancestor.
proposed.matched_by: The positive-lag frontier theorem proves that the bounded-window micro condition is necessary and sufficient for this unadjusted contrast to equal the CDE uniformly over every admissible refinement and every strictly positive model in the present class. The one-lag \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\) witness shows a strict gain over the label-level exclusion.

proposed.comparator_claim: Their response-function construction turns one specified discrete causal model into a polynomial program and obtains numerical valid bounds converging to sharpness.
proposed.matched_by: The sharp-envelope and exact-certification theorems compile the union of all observationally feasible positive-lag refinements, attain both endpoints, reconstruct endpoint SCMs, and return exact algebraic certificates.

proposed.comparator_claim: Their causal-order linear program optimizes counterfactual queries over arbitrary masses on complete deterministic response signatures consistent with the supplied order and reconstructs attaining SCMs.
proposed.matched_by: The order-tightening theorem uses their unrestricted complete-order model as an outer comparator, while the quotient-obstruction theorem shows that arbitrary quotient masses cannot replace independent edge-factor weights in the present semi-Markovian refinement compiler.

proposed.comparator_claim: Proposition 3.1 preserves a canonical-domain linear program by pushing an unrestricted simplex mass to equivalence cells and selecting one raw representative per cell for the reverse lift.
proposed.matched_by: The quotient-obstruction theorem separates that unrestricted-simplex setting from the present independent-edge-latent setting: a full-support rational quotient law violates a factor-incidence polynomial satisfied by every raw product model.

proposed.comparator_claim: Their bounded-segment theorem decides identification in one known periodic bounded-lag ADMG by cutting repeated hedge states.
Their PAG procedure gives sound analytical bounds at least as tight as natural bounds and shows that several graph representatives may remain necessary.
proposed.matched_by: The robust order-tightening theorem gives an explicit temporal micro-CDE family on which summary-graph refinement bounds are strictly narrower than the complete-order outer comparator.

proposed.comparator_claim: Their covering-collection construction gives uniformly valid minimum-average-volume confidence regions for a multinomial parameter.
proposed.matched_by: The simultaneous whole-set inference theorem propagates one multinomial confidence event through all endpoint and same-SCM contrast optimizations.

proposed.comparator_claim: Their root-cause method compares identified direct effects under an acyclic causally sufficient summary graph.
proposed.matched_by: The simultaneous whole-set inference theorem extends comparison to partially identified refinement fibers and reports ties whenever the same-SCM difference interval contains zero.

proposed.comparator_claim: Their real-quantifier-elimination results give arithmetic-operation bounds and output degree and coefficient-size bounds in polynomial count, degree, coefficient height, and variable blocks.
proposed.matched_by: The exact-certification theorem applies those direct arithmetic and size bounds to the causal compiler; its stated bit-operation bound is the derived corollary obtained from the accompanying bit-size control, not a separately quoted source theorem.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The table must reflect the exact uniform frontier for the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast, distinguish independent edge-factor incidence from unrestricted response-signature simplexes, and state honestly which real-algebraic complexity claims are direct and which are derived.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite binary process is observed through a bounded window and a lag-abstracted directed and bidirected summary graph. Directed effects occur only at positive lags through \(L\), while bidirected dependence may span any summary-compatible pair of time points in the observed \(H\)-window. The sharp controlled-micro-direct-effect envelope is the attained range of the raw semi-Markovian polynomial programs over exactly those refinements whose canonical fiber reproduces the observed law; a total exact certifier returns either branchwise incompatibility evidence or isolated algebraic endpoints with attaining SCMs. In the present independent pairwise-edge-latent class, the bounded-window micro condition is necessary and sufficient for the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast to equal the micro CDE uniformly over every admissible refinement and every strictly positive model. This is an exact frontier for that contrast, not a necessary-and-sufficient identification criterion from the full observed law. The condition permits directed summary cycles through \(Y\) and strictly improves the label-level exclusion, as witnessed by the one-lag summary \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\). The envelope is strictly narrower on a relative-open temporal-instrument family than a complete temporal-order comparator, and simultaneous multinomial regions support tie-aware inference. Exact response-signature analysis preserves the image under factorized push-forward, supplies a quotient-size bound and a factor-incidence test, and gives a full-support rational obstruction showing that unrestricted quotient masses erase independent edge-factor incidence; the endpoint compiler therefore retains the raw product parameterization unless the test succeeds.

project_justification.gap: Existing summary-graph adjustment results give sufficient label-level conditions in broader models that may contain contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws; they do not give the exact finite-window frontier for uniform validity of the unadjusted conditional-mean contrast in a positive-lag independent-edge-latent class. Existing automated bounds generally treat one declared graph. Moreover, unrestricted response-signature simplex reductions do not encode the nonlinear incidence constraints imposed by mutually independent overlapping pairwise latent parents, and their failure could previously be dismissed as a boundary-support artifact.
project_justification.niche: The positive-directed-lag bound makes the full-time refinement set finite and makes \(Y_0\) terminal, while summary-compatible bidirected lags remain unrestricted inside the observed window. The bounded positive-lag supergraph exposes exactly when a latent incident to \(Y_0\) can enter the recursive determination of the controlled possible-parent vector. Binary canonical response functions turn every observationally feasible fixed-refinement image into a compact semialgebraic set; the complete temporal-order common-latent model remains a coherent graph-free outer comparator. Retaining the independent latent-factor product structure distinguishes this compiler from unrestricted response-signature simplexes.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a sharp raw compiler over all and only observationally feasible refinements, proves endpoint attainment and SCM reconstruction, and gives a total exact certifier. It proves that the bounded-window micro condition holds if and only if the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast is uniformly correct over every admissible refinement and every strictly positive model in this class; the one-lag \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\) example certifies strict improvement over the label-level exclusion. It separately records that failure of the condition need not destroy identification from the full observed law. Explicit rational primal tables, pointwise dual inequalities, and an interior ledger certify relative-open strict tightening, while one multinomial event is propagated through all queries and contrasts. For response-signature compression, exact factorized push-forward fidelity, a necessary-and-sufficient factor-incidence sentence, a quotient-size bound, and the full-support parity-tilt obstruction explain precisely when unrestricted quotienting is unsound. The exact-elimination analysis uses direct arithmetic-operation and output-size bounds; the bit-operation statement is their derived corollary.

prose_updates.related_work: Ferreira and Assaad (2026, Theorem 9) provide the summary-graph controlled-micro-direct-effect setup and an unadjusted conditional-mean identifying expression under label-level graphical conditions. In the present finite-window binary semi-Markovian class with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents, strict positive lags make \(Y_0\) terminal. The new bounded-window micro condition is exact for a deliberately narrower uniform claim: it holds if and only if \(q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(P_{\mathcal M})\) for every admissible refinement and every strictly positive model in this class. It removes the singleton strongly connected component requirement and the conservative exclusion of every summary bidirected edge to a summary ancestor. With \(H=L=1\), summary arrows \(B\to X\to Y\), and \(Y\leftrightarrow B\), the only \(B\to X\) placement is too late to affect controlled parent \(X_{-1}\), so the new condition holds although the label-level exclusion fails. This exactness concerns the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast, not identification from the entire observed law: with \(H=2\), \(L=\gamma=1\), \(B_{-2}\to X_{-1}\to Y_0\), and \(B_{-2}\leftrightarrow Y_0\), the micro condition fails but adjustment for observed \(B_{-2}\) can still identify the effect. The present scope neither contains nor is contained in Ferreira--Assaad's broader one, because they permit contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws while this paper excludes instantaneous directed effects and imposes independent pairwise-edge-latent factorization. Duarte et al. (2024, Propositions 1--2 and Algorithm 2) provide the canonical response-function and polynomialization method adapted within each refinement; the present sharp union ranges only over refinements with a nonempty canonical fiber, and the total exact real-algebraic layer adds branchwise incompatibility certificates, endpoint isolation, causal-size bounds, and decoded SCM witnesses. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (2025, Propositions 1--2) inform finite-window reasoning for known bounded-lag periodic ADMGs but are not the source of the positive-lag restriction. Rossetto and Antonucci (2026) and Choe et al. (2026) use unrestricted masses on response signatures or equivalence cells. Here push-forward is exact only while the induced factorized quotient family is retained: for rational \(0<\theta<1\), the full-support law \(p_\theta(w)=2^{-N}[1+\theta(-1)^{A_0\mathbin\oplus C_0}]\) belongs to an unrestricted quotient simplex, while the raw independent-edge-latent image satisfies \(F(P)=P_{00}P_{11}-P_{01}P_{10}=0\) and the displayed law has \(F(P)=\theta/4\). Thus the obstruction is not caused by zero observational cells. A finite factor-incidence sentence decides equality, lexicographic minimization gives a semialgebraic selector when equality holds, and the derived quotient-size bound closes the former size question. Evans (2016, Theorem 4.13 and Proposition 7.4) motivates retaining latent-margin structure. Geiger and Meek (1999) and Basu, Pollack, and Roy (1996) supply exact-elimination and complexity ancestors; the arithmetic-operation and output bit-size bounds are used directly, while the theorem's bit-operation complexity is the resulting derived corollary. Bellot (2024, Propositions 3--5) shows that partial graphical information can improve graph-free bounds but does not give the present temporal micro-CDE strictness region. Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2020, Theorem 1) motivate whole-multinomial coverage, while Assaad, Ez-Zejjari, and Zan (2023, Proposition 7 and Theorem 1) supply the downstream direct-effect root-cause comparison made uncertainty-aware by the same-SCM tie rule.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Exact push-forward to response-signature equivalence classes preserves the raw image when the induced factorized quotient family is retained, but this operation alone does not remove the latent product parameterization. The unrestricted branchwise quotient simplex is computationally smaller and is not sound in general. On the edge-latent-chain instance, the rational family \(p_\theta(w)=2^{-N}[1+\theta(-1)^{A_0\mathbin\oplus C_0}]\), \(0<\theta<1\), has every observed cell positive but violates by \(\theta/4\) the independence determinant that vanishes on the raw image. The exact factor-incidence test decides graph by graph whether the unrestricted quotient happens to be safe, and the canonical catalogue has a derived finite quotient-size bound. Consequently the certified endpoint compiler retains raw product weights unless that test succeeds; the remaining limitation is worst-case combinatorial size, not unresolved fidelity, support, or quotient size.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The paper studies finite-window binary SCMs with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents. It excludes instantaneous directed effects and directed lags beyond \(L\), but places no \(L\)-bound on bidirected lags inside the observed \(H\)-window. Ferreira--Assaad allow contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws, so the positive-lag theorem is an extension only within the present distinct scope. Its necessary-and-sufficient claim is exactly a frontier for uniform equality with the unadjusted contrast \(A_{\mathrm{FA}}\), not a necessary-and-sufficient criterion for identification from the full observed law. Indeed, with \(H=2\), \(L=\gamma=1\), summary arrows \(B\to X\to Y\), and \(B\leftrightarrow Y\), a refinement containing \(B_{-2}\to X_{-1}\to Y_0\) and \(B_{-2}\leftrightarrow Y_0\) fails the micro condition, yet the observed \(B_{-2}\) supplies an alternative adjustment route under the usual positivity needed for that conditional formula. The envelope is the smallest closed interval containing all attainable CDE values; the attainable set itself need not be connected. Its nested extrema range only over refinements whose canonical feasible set is nonempty. No stationarity or infinite-history reduction is assumed. Exact certification is worst-case singly exponential in the raw response-weight dimension and is a certificate engine, not a polynomial-time method. Its arithmetic-operation and output bit-size controls come directly from real-algebraic elimination results; its bit-operation complexity is a derived corollary. Empty fibers receive exact branchwise infeasibility certificates, while nonempty fibers receive attained algebraic endpoints and decoded SCMs. Every graph refinement embeds in the complete temporal-order common-latent comparator, but unrestricted comparator masses are not asserted to respect missing bidirected edges. Strict tightening is relative to positive laws with a nonempty summary-graph fiber. The quotient question is resolved: factorized push-forward is exact, a necessary-and-sufficient real-algebraic test characterizes when the unrestricted quotient simplex is also exact, a finite quotient-size bound is proved, and a full-support rational edge-latent-chain witness shows that unrestricted quotienting fails in general. Accordingly the main compiler remains unquotiented unless the exact test certifies a particular graph. When the refinement class is a singleton the construction reduces to a fixed-graph response program.

statement_notes.justification: This is the sharp graphical partial-identification kernel: it equates the summary-graph SCM fiber with an evaluable finite polynomial union over observationally feasible refinements and certifies endpoint SCMs.
statement_notes.gap: Duarte et al. treat one declared discrete causal model, while Ferreira--Assaad supply point identification on a graphical regime; neither gives the sharp union over unknown positive-lag refinements with one common micro CDE.
statement_notes.consumer: An analyst with a cyclic or confounded summary graph can report the smallest valid interval over every observationally compatible lag placement without selecting an unsupported full-time graph.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a rational number \(\theta\) with \(0<\theta<1\).  We first construct the quotient-simplex point.  In \(G_{\mathrm{ABC}}\), take the canonical branch \(r_\star\) in which every private exogenous variable is binary, every pairwise edge exogenous variable is constant, and, for each \(v\in\mathcal W_H\),
\[
f_v\bigl(x_{\operatorname{pa}_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}}}(v)},(u_a:a\ni v)\bigr)=u_{\{v\}}.
\tag{27}
\]
Thus every structural table ignores its observed-parent and pairwise-edge inputs.  This is one of the finite deterministic table systems enumerated by \(\text{def:raw-polynomial-compiler}\); equivalently, its exogenous supports have size at most \(C=2^N+|\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}|\), and the catalogue in \(\text{lem:finite-factor-support-reduction}\) contains its padded deterministic-table branch.

For each \(w\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}\), let \(\omega_w\) be the raw signature in branch \(r_\star\) having \(u_{\{v\}}=w_v\) for every \(v\).  Equation (27) makes its observational recursion equal to \(w\).  It also makes the equation for \(C_0\) ignore the directed parent \(A_{-1}\).  Consequently the singleton query in \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}\) has deterministic contrast zero and
\[
T_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}},\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}}(\omega_w)=(e_w,0).
\tag{28}
\]
Let \(C_w=\pi_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}},\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}}(\omega_w)\).  If \(w\ne w'\), then \(e_w\ne e_{w'}\), so (28) and the definition of \(\sim_{G,\mathcal J}\) give \(C_w\ne C_{w'}\).  Define a mass on the quotient cells of \(r_\star\) by
\[
\nu_\theta(C_w)=p_\theta(w)
=2^{-N}\bigl[1+\theta(-1)^{w_{A_0}\oplus w_{C_0}}\bigr].
\tag{29}
\]
There are two assignments of \((w_{A_0},w_{C_0})\) with parity zero and two with parity one.  For each fixed assignment of the remaining \(N-2\) coordinates, their four contributions to the bracket in (29) sum to \(4\).  Hence
\[
\sum_w p_\theta(w)=1.
\]
Moreover, \(1-\theta>0\), so every \(p_\theta(w)\) is positive; and rationality of \(\theta\) makes every mass rational.  Thus \(\nu_\theta\) is a rational branchwise quotient probability mass and its observed law has full support.  By (28)--(29),
\[
\mathbb E_{\nu_\theta}[\overline T_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}},\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}}]
=(p_\theta,0)=x_\theta,
\]
so \(x_\theta\in\mathcal A_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}},\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}}^{\mathrm{simp-q}}\) by \(\text{def:factorized-quotient-images}\).

We next prove nonmembership in the raw image.  Consider an arbitrary raw canonical parameter point on \(G_{\mathrm{ABC}}\).  By \(\text{def:abc-kill-test-instance}\), \(A_0\) has no observed parent and its only incident pairwise latent is \(U_{A_0B_0}\); hence \(A_0\) is a deterministic function of
\[
\mathcal U_A=(U_{\{A_0\}},U_{A_0B_0}).
\]
The only observed parent of \(C_0\) is \(A_{-1}\), the latter has no observed parent and no incident pairwise latent, and the only pairwise latent incident to \(C_0\) is \(U_{B_0C_0}\).  Therefore \(C_0\) is a deterministic function of
\[
\mathcal U_C=(U_{\{A_{-1}\}},U_{\{C_0\}},U_{B_0C_0}).
\]
The two displayed latent collections are disjoint.  Mutual independence in \(\text{ass:independent-edge-latents}\) therefore makes \(\mathcal U_A\) independent of \(\mathcal U_C\), and summing their product mass over inverse images of the two structural functions gives
\[
\Pr(A_0=i,C_0=j)=\Pr(A_0=i)\Pr(C_0=j),
\qquad i,j\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{30}
\]
Thus every raw observational image obeys
\[
D(P)=P_{00}P_{11}-P_{01}P_{10}=0,
\tag{31}
\]
because substitution of (30) makes both products equal to
\(\Pr(A_0=0)\Pr(A_0=1)\Pr(C_0=0)\Pr(C_0=1)\).

For the law in (29), summing over the \(2^{N-2}\) assignments of the other coordinates gives
\[
(p_\theta)_{ij}
=\frac14\bigl[1+\theta(-1)^{i\oplus j}\bigr].
\tag{32}
\]
Consequently
\[
\begin{aligned}
D(p_\theta)
&=\left(\frac{1+\theta}{4}\right)^2
-\left(\frac{1-\theta}{4}\right)^2\\
&=\frac{\theta}{4}>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{33}
\]
Equations (31)--(33) are an exact rational polynomial nonmembership certificate, so \(x_\theta\notin\mathcal A_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}},\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}}^{\mathrm{raw}}\).  In view of \(\text{lem:factorized-pushforward-fidelity}\), push-forward itself preserves the raw image exactly; the enlargement in (29) occurs only because the unrestricted quotient simplex discards the product-factorization restriction.  This proves the full-support obstruction and alternative \({\rm(ii)}\).

For the general decision statement, fix finite orderings of branches, quotient cells, factors, states, and output coordinates.  For a branch \(r\), let
\[
A_r\nu=\sum_C\nu(C)\overline T_{G,\mathcal J}(C),
\]
and for a branch \(r'\), let
\[
F_{r'}(\lambda)
=\sum_\kappa\left(\prod_a\lambda_a(\kappa_a)\right)
T_{G,\mathcal J}(r',\kappa).
\]
The first map is linear and the second is polynomial.  Simplex membership is given by coordinatewise weak inequalities and one linear equality.  Hence the displayed factor-incidence criterion is the finite first-order real sentence
\[
\bigwedge_r\ \forall\nu\in\Delta(\overline\Omega_r)\ 
\bigvee_{r'}\ \exists\lambda\in\prod_a\Delta(\mathcal K_{G,r',a}):
A_r\nu=F_{r'}(\lambda).
\tag{34}
\]
Here \(\overline\Omega_r\) denotes the quotient cells contained in branch \(r\).  By \(\text{def:factorized-quotient-images}\), the unrestricted quotient image is
\[
\bigcup_r A_r\Delta(\overline\Omega_r),
\]
whereas the raw image is
\[
\bigcup_{r'}F_{r'}\left(\prod_a\Delta(\mathcal K_{G,r',a})\right).
\]
The raw-to-quotient inclusion is \(\text{lem:factorized-pushforward-fidelity}\).  Therefore (34) is equivalent to the reverse inclusion and is necessary and sufficient for equality of the two images.  All coefficients in (34) are rational, indeed integral apart from the simplex normalizations.  Successive elimination of its finitely many quantifier blocks by \(\text{lem:one-block-real-algebraic-elimination}\) decides its truth exactly.

Suppose (34) holds.  For fixed \((r,\nu)\), the feasible raw weights in each candidate branch \(r'\) form the inverse image of the singleton \(\{A_r\nu\}\) under the continuous polynomial map \(F_{r'}\), intersected with a product of finite simplices.  This set is closed and compact.  At least one such set is nonempty by (34).  Choose the first branch with a nonempty fiber and, within that fiber, successively minimize the coordinates of \(\lambda\) in the fixed order.  Compactness gives a minimizer at every step, and the final vector is unique.  The assertion that a branch is the first feasible one, and the assertion that a feasible coordinate is no larger than that of every other point in the remaining fiber, are finite first-order real formulas.  Quantifier elimination therefore makes the graph of this lexicographic choice semialgebraic.  It is a single-valued selector and reconstructs factor weights for every quotient-simplex point whenever (34) holds.

It remains to prove the catalogue-size bound.  Put \(C=2^N+|\mathcal J|\).  By \(\text{lem:finite-factor-support-reduction}\), each exogenous factor may be padded to \(C\) states without changing the attainable image.  A vertex has at most \(N-1\) observed parents and at most \(w_G\) incident exogenous factors.  Its Boolean structural table consequently has at most
\[
2^{N-1}C^{w_G}
\]
input rows and at most \(2^{2^{N-1}C^{w_G}}\) possible values as a whole table.  Across the \(N\) vertices, a duplicate-free normalized catalogue thus has at most
\[
2^{N2^{N-1}C^{w_G}}
\tag{35}
\]
branches.

Let \(m\) be the number of exogenous factors.  There is one private factor per observed vertex and one factor per bidirected edge, so
\[
m=N+|E_G^{\leftrightarrow}|.
\]
Counting incidences of these factors at the observed vertices and using the definition of \(w_G\) gives
\[
N+2|E_G^{\leftrightarrow}|\le Nw_G.
\]
It follows that
\[
m\le\frac{N(w_G+1)}2.
\tag{36}
\]
Thus each branch has at most
\[
C^m\le C^{N(w_G+1)/2}
\]
raw signatures.  Independently, the observational part of \(T_{G,\mathcal J}\) is one of \(2^N\) one-hot vectors, while its query part is one of \(3^{|\mathcal J|}\) vectors in \(\{-1,0,1\}^{\mathcal J}\).  Hence a branch has at most \(2^N3^{|\mathcal J|}\) quotient cells.  The number of its quotient cells is bounded by the smaller of these two quantities.  Multiplication by the branch bound (35) proves
\[
|\overline\Omega_{G,\mathcal J}|
\le
2^{N2^{N-1}C^{w_G}}
\min\left\{C^{N(w_G+1)/2},2^N3^{|\mathcal J|}\right\}.
\]
This completes the obstruction, decision, selector, and size claims.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For \(G_{\mathrm{ABC}}\) and \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}\), the procedure \(\mathsf{QCan}\) returns alternative \({\rm(ii)}\) even at a strictly positive observed law.  More precisely, for every rational \(\theta\) with \(0<\theta<1\), there is a rational branchwise quotient mass \(\nu_\theta\) whose image \(x_\theta\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}},\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}}^{\mathrm{simp-q}}\) but not to \(\mathcal A_{G_{\mathrm{ABC}},\mathcal J_{\mathrm{ABC}}}^{\mathrm{raw}}\), whose query coordinate is zero, and whose observed coordinate is the full-support law
\[
p_\theta(w)=2^{-N}\bigl[1+\theta(-1)^{w_{A_0}\oplus w_{C_0}}\bigr],
\qquad w\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}.
\]
Writing \(P_{ij}=\sum_{w:w_{A_0}=i,\,w_{C_0}=j}P(w)\), the observational polynomial
\[
D(P)=P_{00}P_{11}-P_{01}P_{10}
\]
vanishes throughout the raw image but satisfies \(D(p_\theta)=\theta/4\).  Thus the unrestricted quotient simplex is not factorization-safe even in the interior of the observed probability simplex: freeing quotient-cell masses erases the independent edge-factor incidence constraints, so the endpoint compiler must retain the raw product parameterization on this graph.

For general \(G\) and finite \(\mathcal J\), equality of the raw and unrestricted quotient images is decidable by the following necessary-and-sufficient factor-incidence test: for every branch \(r\) and every mass \(\nu\) on its quotient cells, there must exist a branch \(r'\) and factor weights \(\lambda\in\prod_a\Delta(\mathcal K_{G,r',a})\) such that
\[
\sum_C\nu(C)\overline T_{G,\mathcal J}(C)
=\sum_\kappa\left(\prod_a\lambda_a(\kappa_a)\right)T_{G,\mathcal J}(r',\kappa).
\]
This finite first-order real-algebraic condition is exact; when it holds, lexicographic minimization in its compact fibers gives a semialgebraic selector.  Moreover, the canonical catalogue may be chosen so that, with \(C=2^N+|\mathcal J|\),
\[
|\overline\Omega_{G,\mathcal J}|
\le
2^{N2^{N-1}C^{w_G}}
\min\left\{C^{N(w_G+1)/2},\,2^N3^{|\mathcal J|}\right\}.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing two-cell witness lies on the observed-simplex boundary. The required repair asks for a strictly positive rational obstruction. Strict positivity changes the determinant certificate from the boundary value one quarter to theta divided by four for rational theta strictly between zero and one; the general decision, selector, and quotient-size claims remain unchanged.

proofs.proof_tex:
By \(\text{ass:focal-positive-lag-parent}\),
\[
W=\{X_{-\gamma}\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z.
\tag{C1}
\]
For \(x\in\{0,1\}\), the probability \(p(W=(x,z))\) is a finite sum of full-window cell probabilities.  Every summand is positive by \(\text{ass:strict-observed-positivity}\), and at least one completion exists; hence
\[
p(W=(x,z))>0.
\tag{C2}
\]
Thus both conditionals in \(A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\) are well defined.

Fix \((G,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\).  Its induced law is \(p\) by \(\text{ass:observed-law-compatibility}\), and all other hypotheses in the universal property \(\mathrm{(UA)}\) of \(\text{thm:positive-lag-fa-exact-frontier}\) follow from membership in \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\).  The displayed hypothesis \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) and the forward implication of that theorem therefore give
\[
q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\tag{C3}
\]
The fiber member was arbitrary, so \(\text{def:sharp-envelope}\) yields
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\subseteq\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\}.
\tag{C4}
\]
The assumed nonemptiness of the fiber supplies a member to which (C3) applies, proving the reverse inclusion in (C4).  Hence
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)=\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\}.
\tag{C5}
\]
Taking the infimum and supremum of this nonempty singleton and using \(\text{def:sharp-envelope}\) proves
\[
\underline q(p)=\overline q(p)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\tag{C6}
\]

We next compare \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) with the label-level exclusion in the statement.  Suppose that exclusion holds and, toward a contradiction, let \(b=(B,s)\) belong to the intersection in \(\mathrm{(MC)}\).  The relation \(\{Y_0,b\}\in\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\) implies \(Y\leftrightarrow B\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\leftrightarrow}\).  Ancestry supplies a directed path in \(D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) from \(b\) to some \(w=(C,-\ell)\in W\).  Projection of that path is a directed summary walk from \(B\) to \(C\), with the length-zero case giving \(B=C\).  Since \(w\in W\), the definition of \(W\) gives \(C\to Y\in E_{\mathcal S}^{\to}\).  Concatenation and deletion of repeated vertices give a directed summary path from \(B\) to \(Y\).  Thus \(B\) is a directed summary ancestor of \(Y\), contradicting the label-level exclusion.  Therefore that exclusion implies \(\mathrm{(MC)}\).

The implication is strict.  Let \(H=L=\gamma=1\), take distinct labels \(B,X,Y\), and give the summary graph precisely the directed edges
\[
B\to X,
\qquad
X\to Y,
\tag{C7}
\]
and the bidirected edge \(Y\leftrightarrow B\).  The directed supergraph has only
\[
B_{-1}\to X_0,
\qquad
X_{-1}\to Y_0.
\tag{C8}
\]
Therefore \(W=\{X_{-1}\}\),
\[
\operatorname{An}_{D_{1,1}(\mathcal S)}(W)=\{X_{-1}\},
\tag{C9}
\]
and the endpoints paired with \(Y_0\) in \(\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\), namely \(B_{-1}\) and \(B_0\), do not lie in (C9).  Thus \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) holds, even though \(B\to X\to Y\) makes \(B\) a directed summary ancestor of \(Y\).

To show that this strict gain has a nonempty positive fiber, let \(G^{\star}\) contain the two arrows in (C8) and \(Y_0\leftrightarrow B_{-1}\).  It obeys the positive-lag restriction, its bidirected edge is allowed, and its exact projection is the stated summary graph.  Let \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4)\) be the edge latent and let every vertex have a mutually independent private binary noise with both values of positive probability, all independent of \(U\).  Define
\[
\begin{array}{lll}
B_{-1}=U\mathbin\oplus E_{B,-1},
&B_0=E_{B,0},
&X_{-1}=E_{X,-1},\\
X_0=B_{-1}\mathbin\oplus E_{X,0},
&Y_{-1}=E_{Y,-1},
&Y_0=X_{-1}\mathbin\oplus U\mathbin\oplus E_{Y,0}.
\end{array}
\tag{C10}
\]
These equations satisfy structural recursion and independent-edge-latent factorization.  For any observed six-bit cell, fix \(U=0\) and solve (C10) for the six private noises.  The resulting finite latent configuration has positive probability, so the observed law \(p^{\star}\) is strictly positive.  Consequently
\[
(G^{\star},\mathcal M^{\star})\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,1,1,p^{\star}),
\tag{C11}
\]
which proves the advertised nonemptiness.

Finally, directed summary cycles through \(Y\) are compatible with the theorem.  For \(H=L=\gamma=1\), take the two-label summary with directed edges \(X\to Y\) and \(Y\to X\), and no bidirected edges.  The full-time graph with arrows \(X_{-1}\to Y_0\) and \(Y_{-1}\to X_0\) belongs to the refinement class: each arrow advances time, although its projection is cyclic.  Condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) is vacuous.  Equations
\[
X_{-1}=E_{X,-1},
\quad
Y_{-1}=E_{Y,-1},
\quad
X_0=Y_{-1}\mathbin\oplus E_{X,0},
\quad
Y_0=X_{-1}\mathbin\oplus E_{Y,0},
\tag{C12}
\]
with independent two-sided private noises generate a strictly positive law by the same solve-for-the-private-noises argument used for (C10).  Thus a cyclic summary has a nonempty positive fiber satisfying \(\mathrm{(MC)}\), while its positive-lag full-time refinement remains acyclic.

added_lemmas.statement:
Put
\[
\mathrm{(MC)}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bigl\{b\in\mathcal W_H:\{Y_0,b\}\in\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\bigr\}
\cap\operatorname{An}_{D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}(W)=\varnothing.
\]
For the fixed query \((X_{-\gamma},Y_0,z)\), define the universal unadjusted-adjustment property
\[
\mathrm{(UA)}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p_{\mathcal M})
\]
for every \(G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) and every finite binary semi-Markovian model \(\mathcal M\) on \(G\) satisfying structural recursion and mutually independent private and pairwise-edge exogenous variables, whenever its induced observational law \(p_{\mathcal M}\) obeys \(p_{\mathcal M}(a)>0\) for every \(a\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}\).  Then
\[
\mathrm{(MC)}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathrm{(UA)}.
\]
This equivalence is an exact frontier for universal equality with the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast, not a necessary-and-sufficient criterion for identification from the full observed law.  Indeed, with \(H=2\), \(L=\gamma=1\), summary edges \(B\to X\to Y\) and \(B\leftrightarrow Y\), the refinement having \(B_{-2}\to X_{-1}\to Y_0\) and \(B_{-2}\leftrightarrow Y_0\) violates \(\mathrm{(MC)}\), but every strictly positive model on that refinement satisfies
\[
q(\mathcal M)=
\sum_{b\in\{0,1\}}
\Bigl\{
\mathbb E_{p_{\mathcal M}}[Y_0\mid X_{-1}=1,B_{-2}=b]
-
\mathbb E_{p_{\mathcal M}}[Y_0\mid X_{-1}=0,B_{-2}=b]
\Bigr\}p_{\mathcal M}(B_{-2}=b).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We first prove sufficiency.  Assume \(\mathrm{(MC)}\), fix \(G\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\), and fix a model \(\mathcal M\) quantified in \(\mathrm{(UA)}\).  Let \(p_{\mathcal M}\) be its induced observational law.  By its definition, \(\mathcal M\) satisfies \(\text{ass:observed-law-compatibility}\) with \(p=p_{\mathcal M}\); the hypotheses defining \(\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\), together with structural recursion and independent edge latents, therefore give
\[
(G,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p_{\mathcal M}).
\tag{F1}
\]
The stipulated positivity of \(p_{\mathcal M}\) is exactly \(\text{ass:strict-observed-positivity}\).  Applying \(\text{lem:positive-lag-cyclic-cde-adjustment}\) to (F1) yields
\[
q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p_{\mathcal M}).
\tag{F2}
\]
Since \(G\) and \(\mathcal M\) were arbitrary, (F2) proves \(\mathrm{(UA)}\).

For necessity, suppose that \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) fails.  By \(\text{def:bounded-window-micro-ancestry}\), there are a vertex \(b\in\mathcal W_H\), a vertex \(w\in W\), and a directed path
\[
v_0=b\to v_1\to\cdots\to v_m=w
\quad\text{in }D_{H,L}(\mathcal S),
\qquad
\{Y_0,b\}\in\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S).
\tag{F3}
\]
Choose such a path with the least possible number of edges.  Then
\[
v_i\notin W\quad(0\le i<m),
\tag{F4}
\]
because otherwise its prefix would be a shorter path from \(b\) to \(W\).  The case \(m=0\), where \(b=w\), is included.

We construct an admissible refinement.  Include in its directed edge set every edge of the path in (F3) and the focal edge \(X_{-\gamma}\to Y_0\), which is allowed by \(\text{ass:focal-positive-lag-parent}\).  For every directed summary edge not yet represented, add its lag-one placement \((u,-1)\to(v,0)\).  Include the bidirected edge \(Y_0\leftrightarrow b\), and for every bidirected summary edge not yet represented choose one pair of distinct time-indexed endpoints allowed by \(\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\).  Such padding is possible because \(H\ge L\ge1\).  Every directed edge just chosen advances time by between one and \(L\) steps, so the directed part is acyclic.  No edge projects outside \(\mathcal S\), and every summary edge has a representative.  Thus the resulting graph, denoted \(G^{\dagger}\), satisfies
\[
G^{\dagger}\in\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S).
\tag{F5}
\]
The padded edges will be structurally inert.

Let \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) be the exogenous variable for the edge \(Y_0\leftrightarrow b\).  Give every other bidirected edge an independent fair binary exogenous variable.  Give every observed vertex \(a\) an independent binary private variable \(E_a\), independently of all edge variables.  Along the path take
\[
\Pr(E_{v_i}=1)=\frac14,
\qquad 0\le i\le m,
\tag{F6}
\]
and define
\[
V_{v_0}=U\mathbin\oplus E_{v_0},
\qquad
V_{v_i}=V_{v_{i-1}}\mathbin\oplus E_{v_i}quad(1\le i\le m).
\tag{F7}
\]
For each controlled vertex in \(W\setminus\{w\}\), set \(V_a=E_a\) with \(E_a\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\).  This prescription is consistent with (F7) by (F4).  At every remaining vertex other than \(Y_0\), use the same fair-private-noise equation unless (F7) already defines it.  All actual parents and nonspecial edge latents may be ignored by these structural tables, as announced when padding the graph.

Let \(E_0\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4)\) be the private variable at \(Y_0\).  Because \(W=\{X_{-\gamma}\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z\), exactly one of the following cases holds.  Define the terminal equation by
\[
V_{Y_0}=
\begin{cases}
(V_{X_{-\gamma}}\mathbin\vee U)\mathbin\oplus E_0,
&w=X_{-\gamma},\\[2mm]
(V_{X_{-\gamma}}\mathbin\wedge U)\mathbin\oplus E_0,
&w\in Z.
\end{cases}
\tag{F8}
\]
The focal edge in \(G^{\dagger}\) and the special bidirected edge make every argument in (F8) a permitted structural argument.  Equations (F6)--(F8), the inert equations, and mutual independence give a finite binary model \(\mathcal M^{\dagger}\) satisfying \(\text{ass:structural-recursion}\) and \(\text{ass:independent-edge-latents}\).

This model has full observed support.  To see this, fix any observed cell \(a\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}\) and fix every edge latent, including \(U\), at zero; that edge-latent configuration has positive probability.  For every vertex \(v\), its equation has the form
\[
V_v=h_v(V_{\operatorname{pa}_{G^{\dagger}}(v)},(U_e:e\ni v))\mathbin\oplus E_v.
\tag{F9}
\]
Set \(E_v=a_v\mathbin\oplus h_v(a_{\operatorname{pa}_{G^{\dagger}}(v)},0)\).  Every private variable takes either value with positive probability, and there are finitely many mutually independent exogenous variables.  The latent configuration just specified therefore has positive probability and generates \(a\).  Consequently
\[
p_{\mathcal M^{\dagger}}(a)>0
\quad\text{for every }a\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}.
\tag{F10}
\]

It remains to calculate the two contrasts exactly.  Put
\[
R=E_{v_0}\mathbin\oplus\cdots\mathbin\oplus E_{v_m},
\qquad
\kappa=\prod_{i=0}^{m}\bigl(1-2\Pr(E_{v_i}=1)\bigr)=2^{-(m+1)}.
\tag{F11}
\]
Independence in \(\text{ass:independent-edge-latents}\) and (F6) give
\[
\Pr(R=1)=r:=\frac{1-\kappa}{2}<\frac12,
\qquad
V_w=U\mathbin\oplus R.
\tag{F12}
\]
Since \(U\) is fair and independent of \(R\), \(V_w\) is fair and Bayes' formula, whose denominators are \(1/2>0\), gives
\[
\Pr(U=1\mid V_w=0)=r,
\qquad
\Pr(U=1\mid V_w=1)=1-r.
\tag{F13}
\]
All coordinates of \(W\setminus\{w\}\) are independent fair private variables, so conditioning on them does not alter (F13).

If \(w=X_{-\gamma}\), intervention on \(W\) leaves \(U\) fair.  From the first equation in (F8),
\[
q(\mathcal M^{\dagger})
=\left(1-2\Pr(E_0=1)\right)\left(1-\Pr(U=1)\right)
=\frac14.
\tag{F14}
\]
Observationally, the OR input equals one throughout the arm \(X_{-\gamma}=1\), while (F13) applies in the arm \(X_{-\gamma}=0\).  Hence
\[
A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p_{\mathcal M^{\dagger}})
=\frac12(1-r)
=\frac14+\frac{\kappa}{4}
\ne q(\mathcal M^{\dagger}).
\tag{F15}
\]
If \(w\in Z\), write \(z_w\) for the fixed component of \(z\), and put \(\pi_{z_w}=r\) when \(z_w=0\) and \(\pi_{z_w}=1-r\) when \(z_w=1\).  The second equation in (F8) gives
\[
q(\mathcal M^{\dagger})=\frac14,
\qquad
A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p_{\mathcal M^{\dagger}})=\frac12\pi_{z_w},
\qquad
\left|A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p_{\mathcal M^{\dagger}})-q(\mathcal M^{\dagger})\right|=\frac{\kappa}{4}>0.
\tag{F16}
\]
Thus failure of \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) supplies an admissible full-support rational model violating \(\mathrm{(UA)}\).  This proves \(\mathrm{(UA)}\Rightarrow\mathrm{(MC)}\), and (F2) proves the converse.

Finally, we prove the stated delimitation from full-law identification.  Set \(H=2\), \(L=\gamma=1\), take distinct labels \(B,X,Y\), and let \(G^{\mathrm{alt}}\) have precisely the nonisolated edges
\[
B_{-2}\to X_{-1}\to Y_0,
\qquad
B_{-2}\leftrightarrow Y_0.
\tag{F17}
\]
Its projection has summary directed edges \(B\to X\to Y\) and bidirected edge \(B\leftrightarrow Y\), so \(G^{\mathrm{alt}}\in\mathfrak G_{2,1}(\mathcal S)\).  Here \(W=\{X_{-1}\}\), and \(B_{-2}\to X_{-1}\) in \(D_{2,1}(\mathcal S)\); the endpoint \(B_{-2}\) in (F17) therefore witnesses failure of \(\mathrm{(MC)}\).

Consider any strictly positive semi-Markovian model on \(G^{\mathrm{alt}}\).  Writing \(U_{BY}\) for the edge latent and \(U_B,U_X,U_Y\) for the relevant private latents, structural recursion has the form
\[
B_{-2}=f_B(U_B,U_{BY}),
\quad
X_{-1}=f_X(B_{-2},U_X),
\quad
Y_0=f_Y(X_{-1},U_Y,U_{BY}).
\tag{F18}
\]
Mutual independence of the four exogenous variables implies
\[
U_X\ \perp\ (B_{-2},U_Y,U_{BY}),
\quad\text{and hence}\quad
X_{-1}\ \perp\ (U_Y,U_{BY})\mid B_{-2}.
\tag{F19}
\]
For \(x\in\{0,1\}\), define the intervened response \(Y_0(x)=f_Y(x,U_Y,U_{BY})\).  Equation (F19) gives \(Y_0(x)\perp X_{-1}\mid B_{-2}\), and structural recursion gives \(Y_0(x)=Y_0\) on \(\{X_{-1}=x\}\).  Strict positivity makes every conditional below well defined.  Iterated finite summation, conditional independence, and this consistency identity yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E[Y_0\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-1}=x)]
&=\sum_{b\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E[Y_0(x)\mid B_{-2}=b]p(B_{-2}=b)\\
&=\sum_{b\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E[Y_0(x)\mid X_{-1}=x,B_{-2}=b]p(B_{-2}=b)\\
&=\sum_{b\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E[Y_0\mid X_{-1}=x,B_{-2}=b]p(B_{-2}=b).
\end{aligned}
\tag{F20}
\]
Subtracting (F20) at \(x=0\) from its value at \(x=1\) proves the displayed alternative-adjustment formula.  Hence failure of \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) rules out universal equality with the unadjusted contrast, as (F3)--(F16) prove, but does not by itself rule out identification by another functional of the full observed law.
added_lemmas.justification: The bounded-window ancestry condition is exactly the graphical frontier for universal equality with the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast across all admissible positive refinements and models.
added_lemmas.gap: The converse is deliberately contrast-specific: failure permits a full-support model on which the unadjusted contrast is wrong, while a displayed two-lag graph shows that another observed-law adjustment may still identify the causal effect.
added_lemmas.consumer: The collapse theorem uses the forward direction, and analysts use the converse to distinguish maximality of this simple contrast from the stronger and generally false claim of a complete identification criterion.

proposed.statement:
Suppose \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\ne\varnothing\) and
\[
\bigl\{b\in\mathcal W_H:\{Y_0,b\}\in\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\bigr\}
\cap\operatorname{An}_{D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)}(W)=\varnothing.
\tag{MC}
\]
Then every \((G,\mathcal M)\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal S,L,H,p)\) satisfies \(q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\), and
\[
\Theta(\mathcal S,L,H,p)=\{A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p)\},
\qquad
\underline q(p)=\overline q(p)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(p).
\]
Condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) is strictly weaker than excluding every summary bidirected edge between \(Y\) and a directed summary ancestor of \(Y\).  In particular, a strict-gain instance has \(H=L=\gamma=1\), three distinct component labels \(B,X,Y\), summary directed edges \(B\to X\to Y\), and summary bidirected edge \(Y\leftrightarrow B\): condition \(\mathrm{(MC)}\) holds and the fiber is nonempty for a strictly positive observed law, although \(B\) is a directed summary ancestor of \(Y\).  Directed cycles through \(Y\) also remain permitted.
proposed.justification: The theorem records the singleton sharp-envelope face, while its load-bearing frontier theorem proves that the bounded-window condition is exact for universal equality with the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast.
proposed.gap: This is maximality of one explicit contrast, not a necessary-and-sufficient full-law identification criterion: when the condition fails, an alternative observed adjustment can still identify the effect, as the two-lag counterexample proves.
proposed.consumer: Users obtain the unadjusted contrast and collapsed sharp envelope exactly on its universal graphical regime, while retaining other identification methods when that regime fails.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the exact universal unadjusted-adjustment frontier into the owned collapse theorem and update its node-level positioning without changing the frozen collapse claim.
